claims.text: Setting an environment variable on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service lets Terraform and OpenTofu use the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud as a state backend.
The `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` environment variable on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service sets the domain that serves the Terraform-compatible API.
When `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` is unset on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service, the Terraform-compatible API is disabled and its routes aren't registered.
The DNS record for the `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` domain should point at the same host that serves `PULUMI_API_DOMAIN` in a self-hosted Pulumi Cloud.
In a self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` can be set to the same value as `PULUMI_API_DOMAIN`, so a separate domain is not required for the Terraform-compatible API.

The Terraform state backend guide at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ uses `tf.pulumi.com` as the domain in the Terraform/OpenTofu configuration, the `terraform login`/`tofu login` command, and the `TF_TOKEN_*` variable name.
For self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, the `TF_TOKEN_*` variable name uses the `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` value as the domain.
